input.requirements: unique takes an array of numbers or strings and returns a new array containing only the first occurrence of each distinct value, in original order. Number 1 and string "1" remain distinct. Do not mutate the input. Empty arrays return empty. Non-array inputs throw TypeError.

context.content: export function unique(xs){if(!Array.isArray(xs))throw new TypeError();return [...new Set(xs)];}

tasks.instructions: Create test/unique.test.js using node:test and node:assert/strict, importing unique from ../src/unique.js. Derive explicit expected arrays from the supplied requirements. Test first-occurrence deduplication and original order with repeated numbers, repeated strings, and mixed values where 1 and "1" remain distinct. Cover empty arrays, singleton arrays, all-duplicate arrays, and already-distinct arrays. Assert every successful result is a new array, including empty and already-distinct inputs. Verify input contents remain unchanged and frozen valid arrays are accepted. Assert TypeError for representative non-array inputs: undefined, null, numbers, strings, booleans, plain objects, and array-like objects. Keep tests deterministic and runnable in the supplied ESM project; do not construct expected results using Set or duplicate the implementation.
